title: Understanding LASSO Regularization
text: LASSO regularization adds a penalty term to the loss function, which is proportional to the absolute value of the coefficients. This can lead to some coefficients being exactly zero, effectively selecting a simpler model.

title: Effect on Model Bias
text: Consider how adding a penalty term to the loss function might affect the bias of the model. Remember, bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model.

title: Effect on Model Variance
text: Think about how LASSO regularization, which can shrink coefficients towards zero, might affect the variance of the model. Variance refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training data.

title: Effect on MSE (Training Data)
text: Consider how the introduction of a penalty term might affect the Mean Squared Error (MSE) on the training data. Remember, MSE is a measure of the average of the squares of the errors—that is, the average squared difference between the estimated values and the actual value.

title: Effect on MSE (Test Data)
text: Think about how LASSO regularization might affect the Mean Squared Error (MSE) on held-out test data. Consider the trade-off between bias and variance and how it might impact the model's performance on unseen data.
